items.example: It seems that the shop closes earlier on Saturdays.

note.en: Softens a statement you are not completely sure about.
note.es: Suaviza algo de lo que no estás del todo seguro.

items.example: Perhaps we could meet after the lecture instead of before it.
It's a bit expensive for a student, isn't it?

note.en: Politely understates a complaint. 'A bit' is stronger than it sounds.
note.es: Rebaja una queja con educación. «A bit» suena a más de lo que dice.

items.example: In some ways, living in a small village is easier than living in a city.
Public transport tends to be crowded in the early evening.
To some extent, the weather decides how many people visit the park.
I suppose most people would rather pay online than queue at the bank.
As far as I know, the library opens at nine on weekdays.

note.en: Shows your information may be incomplete.
note.es: Indica que tu información puede estar incompleta.

items.example: It could be argued that remote work has made teams more productive.

note.en: Presents a view without saying it is yours. Very useful in Writing part 4.
note.es: Presenta una idea sin decir que es tuya. Muy útil en Writing 4.

items.phrase: This would appear to suggest that …
items.example: This would appear to suggest that customers value speed above price.

note.en: Cautious wording for conclusions from evidence.
note.es: Fórmula cauta para sacar conclusiones de datos.

items.example: It is somewhat surprising that the scheme attracted so few applicants.
By and large, residents are happy with the new recycling centre.

note.en: Means in most cases, with a few exceptions.

items.example: I'm not sure, but I think the shop closes at six.
It depends. I like it when the weather is nice.
